factual_check.conclusion: Reference is factually sound: FPR=FP/(FP+TN), precision=TP/(TP+FP), ROC-AUC integrates threshold-dependent ROC performance. At fixed TPR/FPR, changing positive prevalence changes precision.
factual_check.derived_example: For 100 positives and 99900 negatives, TPR=0.9 and FPR=0.01 give TP=90, FP=999 and precision=90/1089, about 8.26%. This operating point alone does not establish the entire ROC-AUC.

rubric_findings.description: Question asks why ROC-AUC can be high while precision is low, not which diagnostic to use. Prevalence is essential, but requiring a PR-curve recommendation for 33 points risks rewarding unsolicited advice. Current system prompt says not to require reference material beyond the question. Scores below follow the existing rubric for comparability, not endorsement of its scope.
